# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 64 (Bu-Vb Pc64)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc64
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 64
**Title (English, from literature):** Concealing a grave offense
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

**Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 64** (*Duṭṭhulla-sikkhāpada*), located in the Sappāṇakavagga of the Vinaya Piṭaka (Vin IV 127), establishes a rule concerning the concealment of another monk's serious monastic breach [Hüsken 1997]. The rule dictates that a bhikkhu who knowingly conceals another bhikkhu's grave offense (*duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ*) commits a *pācittiya*, an offense requiring confession [Blackstone 1995; Hüsken 1997]. The accompanying word analysis (*padabhājana*) defines a "grave offense" in this context as specifically comprising *pārājika* and *saṅghādisesa* offenses [Hüsken 1997]. Commentators and modern scholars highlight a distinct gender asymmetry in Vinaya jurisprudence: whereas a monk concealing a fault of the highest order incurs only a relatively minor *pācittiya* requiring confession and no formal disciplinary proceedings (*mānatta*), a nun concealing a major offense commits Bhikkhunī Pārājika 2 (*vajjapaṭicchādikā*), which results in complete expulsion from the order [Blackstone 1995; Hüsken 1997].

 In Pali, it corresponds directly to Bhikkhu Pātimokkha Pācittiya 64 and Bhikkhu Parivāra Pācittiya 64. The text is translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
